### Shattuck Labs Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Business Highlights


November 5, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s21.q4cdn.com/754780530/files/doc_news/Shattuck-Labs-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-and-Recent-Business-Highlights-2026.pdf)


– *Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in Crohn’s disease; 12-week induction data expected in the first half of 2028 –*


*– Announced RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in hidradenitis suppurativa; trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 –*


*– Presented preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from a chronic toxicology study in non-human primates –*


AUSTIN, Texas and DURHAM, N.C., Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shattuck Labs, Inc. (Shattuck or the Company) (NASDAQ: STTK), a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of potential first-in-class monoclonal and bispecific DR3 blocking antibodies for the treatment of patients with inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided recent business highlights.


“We are very excited to begin Phase 2 clinical development with SL-325 in both Crohn’s disease and hidradenitis suppurativa. We believe these two studies will allow direct comparisons with the TL1A antibody class and evaluate the efficacy that may be left on the table due to the potential immunogenicity liabilities of TL1A antibodies,” said Taylor Schreiber, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Shattuck. “In addition, SL-846 has demonstrated a compelling profile in preclinical studies, and we expect to share initial Phase 1 clinical data for what we expect to be a first-in-class DR3 by IL-23 receptor blocking antibody in 2027.”


**DR3 Program Development in 2026**


Shattuck is advancing a pipeline of DR3-targeted monoclonal and bispecific antibody product candidates for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases.


Recent updates and anticipated upcoming milestones include:


**SL-325**


Shattuck’s lead clinical-stage product candidate, SL-325, is a potentially first-in-class DR3 blocking antibody for the treatment of Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), and other inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Phase 1 clinical trial results demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability, potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity with an antidrug antibody rate of 3.7%, and highly durable inhibition of TL1A binding to DR3 that may enable quarterly maintenance dosing.


- Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderately-to-severely active Crohn's disease.


- Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate three dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 232 patients, randomized 1:1:1:1.
- Primary endpoint is endoscopic response at 12 weeks. These data are expected in the first half of 2028.


- Announced plans to initiate the RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa, with trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.


- HS is the second Phase 2 indication for SL-325 and expands development beyond IBD.
- Submitted an Investigational New Drug (IND) application to the FDA in October 2026.
- Designed RECEPTIVE-HS1 as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating two dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 150 patients, randomized 1:1:1.
- Primary endpoint is HiSCR50 response at Week 16, with data expected in the first half of 2028.


- Appointed Shoba Ravichandran, M.D., as Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, to lead the clinical development of SL-325 in HS. Dr. Ravichandran brings more than 20 years of drug development experience, including leading the global approval of Cosentyx in HS at Novartis.


**SL-846**
Shattuck’s lead bispecific product candidate, SL-846, is a potentially first-in-class, half-life extended DR3 x IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking antibody for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases.


- Presented preliminary preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from the GLP toxicology study in non-human primates, which showed the following:


- Well tolerated through the top dose of 100 mg/kg.
- No evidence of DR3 or IL-23R agonism.
- Full and durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3, and complete blockade of IL-23 signaling.
- Data from the NHP study support potential quarterly subcutaneous dosing in humans.
- NHP and *in silico* analyses suggest that SL-846 may have a superior immunogenicity profile to TL1A directed bispecific antibodies; projected human anti-drug antibody rate of between 8-12%.


- Shattuck expects to initiate a Phase 1 healthy volunteer clinical trial of SL-846 and report initial data in 2027.


**Upcoming Events**


- **Shattuck plans to participate in the following upcoming events. Details will be included on the Events & Presentations section of the Company’s website.**
- **Evercore ISI 9th Annual Healthcare Conference, November 30-December 1, 2026** . Management will participate in a fireside chat, and in one-on-one meetings.
- **Piper Sandler 38th Annual Healthcare Conference, December 2-3, 2026.** Taylor Schreiber, M.D., Ph.D., CEO of Shattuck Labs will present at the conference, and management will participate in one-on-one meetings.


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results**


- **Cash and Cash Equivalents and Investments:** As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments were $196.3 million, as compared to $86.1 million as of September 30, 2025.
- **Research and Development (R&D) Expenses:** R&D expenses were $21.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $7.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
- **General and Administrative (G&A) Expenses:** G&A expenses were $5.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $4.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
- **Net Loss:** Net loss was $25.2 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, or $0.14 per basic and diluted share, as compared to a net loss of $10.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, or $0.14 per basic and diluted share.


**Financial Guidance**


As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments, were $196.3 million. Shattuck’s current cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments are expected to fund operations into 2029. This cash runway guidance is based on the Company’s current operational plans and excludes any additional capital that may be received, proceeds from business development transactions, and/or additional costs associated with clinical development activities that may be undertaken.


**About SL-325**


SL-325 is a potentially first-in-class Death Receptor 3 (DR3) blocking antibody designed to achieve a complete and durable blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A pathway. Shattuck’s preclinical studies demonstrated high affinity binding and superior activity over TL1A antibodies, and provided a data-driven rationale for targeting the TNF receptor, DR3, versus its ligand, TL1A. SL-325 is a fully Fc-silenced, fully human immunoglobulin G monoclonal antibody. In a Phase 1 clinical trial, SL-325 demonstrated a favorable safety profile, a potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity profile, no evidence of residual DR3 agonism, and provided durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3 at low doses. SL-325 is being evaluated in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with Crohn’s disease, with data from the induction portion of the trial expected in the first half of 2028. We also expect to evaluate SL-325 in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa, with data from the primary treatment portion of the trial expected in the first half of 2028.


**About SL-846**


SL-846 is a potentially first-in-class Death Receptor 3 (DR3) by IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking bispecific antibody designed to achieve complete and durable blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A and IL-23/IL-23R pathways. Shattuck’s preclinical studies demonstrate high affinity binding to both DR3 and IL-23R, with equivalent or superior *in vitro* potency in comparison to benchmark IL-23 controls (sequence equivalents of risankizumab and icotrokinra) in a variety of preclinical assays. SL-846 is an Fc-silenced, half-life extended, fully human immunoglobulin G bispecific antibody that has been evaluated for safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, and pharmacodynamics in an IND-enabling GLP toxicology study in non-human primates.


**About Shattuck Labs, Inc.**


Shattuck Labs, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of potentially first-in-class monoclonal and bispecific DR3 blocking antibodies for the treatment of patients with inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Shattuck’s expertise in protein engineering and the development of novel TNF receptor therapeutics come together in its lead program, SL-325, a potentially first-in-class DR3 blocking antibody designed to achieve a more complete blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A pathway. The Company has offices in both Austin, Texas and Durham, North Carolina. For more information, please visit: www.ShattuckLabs.com.
